test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which year was English education formally introduced in India by the British?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**1835**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formal introduction of **English education** in India by the British took place in the year **1835**.
 
• This decision was largely influenced by the ideas of **Thomas Babington Macaulay**, who advocated for the promotion of English education in his famous **Minute on Education**.
 
• Macaulay argued that English education would create a class of Indians who were **"Indian in blood and color, but English in taste, opinions, morals, and intellect."**
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** had earlier allowed for the allocation of funds to promote education in India, but it was in **1835** that the focus shifted explicitly to English education.
 
• As a result of this shift, the British introduced English as the medium of instruction in schools and colleges, particularly in higher education.
 
• Institutions such as the **Calcutta Medical College** (established in 1835) began using English as the primary medium of teaching.
 
• This marked the beginning of a significant cultural and educational transformation in India, with English becoming a key language for administration, education, and intellectual discourse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1813**__

 __
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** marked the first step by the British to involve themselves in the promotion of education in India.
 
• It allocated a sum of **1 lakh rupees annually** for the "revival and promotion of literature" and the introduction of "useful knowledge" in India.
 
• However, no specific emphasis on English education was made under this act.
 
 
 
• **1854**__
 __
 
• The year **1854** is significant for the **Wood's Despatch**, which laid the foundation for the modern education system in India.
 
• It recommended the establishment of **universities in Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras** and proposed a system of education at all levels (primary, secondary, and higher).
 
• The despatch also emphasized the use of both English and vernacular languages in education.
 
 
 
• **1829**__
 
 
• The year **1829** is historically significant for the abolition of **Sati** under the efforts of **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** and Governor-General **Lord William Bentinck**.
 
• It does not directly relate to the introduction of English education in India.
